Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV. Reviewed briefly and looks like a good mix. A couple clarifying asks before our model-fit run:

1) Edge cases we want included (examples to add to the CSV):
   - Extremely short/underspecified queries ("Help")
   - Contradictory context across turns (customer corrects earlier info)
   - Detection of policy-sensitive content disguised in legalese
   - Prompts that mix multiple intents (billing + technical)

2) Redaction guidance — suggested approach from Redwood for evaluation:
   - Replace direct identifiers with canonical tokens (e.g., [CUSTOMER_NAME], [ACCOUNT_ID]) to preserve context signals.
   - For account numbers that are partially informative (last 4 digits), we recommend replacing with [ACCOUNT_LAST4] rather than full removal.
   - Do not remove product/feature names unless they are PII.

3) Expected outputs — please mark 10 examples as "gold" with a short expected_output_short so we can run strict precision/recall checks.

4) Sharing logs — if you can share a small set of anonymized transcripts (already attached is one), that will help calibrate conversation length distributions.

We'll start with 3 model variants in parallel for the initial evaluation: redwood-4o (quality-first), redwood-2b-quant (cost-friendly), and a tuned redwood-3b-safety variant. Dev and I will run benchmarks and circle back with P95 latency, token-cost estimates, and qualitative failure cases.

Can Priya confirm the Tue 2026-07-14 EOD timeline for the completed CSV? If that works, we'll aim to deliver initial results by Fri 2026-07-17.

Thanks — I’ll also drop an invite for the Wed sync.

Marissa / team — quick technical notes ahead of our run tomorrow:

Summary of recommended evaluation plan:
- Models to test: redwood-4o (baseline quality), redwood-3b-safety (safety-tuned), redwood-2b-quant (quantized, cost-optimized).
- Metrics: P95 latency (local region), tokenized cost per 1k prompts, strict QA precision on gold set, hallucination rate on tricky queries.
- Test set: use the filled CSV + 10 anonymized transcripts (if available). We’ll also generate paraphrase-augmented variants to stress multi-turn robustness.

Benchmarks & tradeoffs (high level):
- redwood-4o: best quality & safety profile but ~2–3x cost vs 2b-quant; expected P95 in our Hosted env ~180–220ms depending on prefix length.
- redwood-3b-safety: good middle ground for safety-sensitive flows; slight drop in coverage on rare KB facts, much cheaper than 4o.
- redwood-2b-quant: ~40–50% cost saving, latency will be slightly better, but expect more calibration work and higher hallucination on ambiguous prompts.

Quality regression concerns / checks:
- If you have previous model outputs or SLA baselines, share them — we’ll run regression tests against the gold set and flag any delta >= 5% precision drop.
- Watch for context-window truncation issues in multi-turn examples. We’ll report top failure modes with sample prompts and system logs.

Redaction / PII handling (practical):
- For evaluation, use tokenized placeholders as Marissa suggested. We will also run a small experiment with real masked tokens vs placeholders to measure impact on model outputs (sometimes placeholders change model phrasing).
- If ACME prefers, we can run a comparison table in the deliverable showing outputs with: (a) full redaction, (b) partial last4 preserved, (c) no redaction (internal-only test).

Deliverables by Fri 2026-07-17 (tentative):
1) Benchmark report (PDF) with latency/cost/QA metrics + top 10 failure cases (we’ll attach model_benchmark_report.pdf).
2) Short recommended config for production (model variant, batching, prefix caching rules).
3) Suggested redaction policy for serving vs evaluation.

One ask for ACME: please mark 10 "gold" rows in the CSV (as Marissa requested) and highlight any prompts that must not be shared outside your org for compliance reasons. Also confirm whether you want us to retain anonymized evaluation logs for 30 days (default) or a shorter retention window.

I’ll start the runs first thing tomorrow and ping here with links to the initial results folder.

Cheers,
